exercises.name: Knee Push-Up
exercises.description: A push-up with the knees on the floor. It shortens the lever so you can practise the push-up pattern with good form.
instructions: Start on hands and knees with hands slightly wider than shoulders.
Walk your knees back until your body forms a straight line from head to knees.
Lower your chest toward the floor with elbows about 45 degrees from your body.
Press the floor away until your arms are straight.
formTips: Squeeze your glutes and brace your core so your hips do not sag.
Keep your neck long and look at a spot just ahead of your hands.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips drop toward the floor.
Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a wall or a high surface and stand further from it to lower the difficulty.

progressions.text: Move to an incline push-up with hands on a chair or bench.
Progress to a full push-up.

exercises.name: Incline Push-Up
exercises.description: A push-up with your hands raised on a stable surface. The higher the surface, the easier it is.
instructions: Place your hands on a sturdy bench, table edge or chair, slightly wider than your shoulders.
Step your feet back until your body is one straight line.
Lower your chest to the edge of the surface.
Press back up without letting your hips sag.
formTips: Make sure the surface cannot slide or tip.
Lower the surface height over the weeks as you get stronger.
commonMistakes: Using an unstable surface such as a rolling chair.
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears.
exercises.beginnerModification: Stand closer to the surface and use a higher one, or do the movement against a wall.

progressions.text: Lower the surface height a little at a time.
Move to a full push-up on the floor.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.description: The classic bodyweight pressing exercise. It trains the chest, shoulders and triceps while your core keeps the body rigid.
instructions: Place your hands slightly wider than your shoulders and step your feet back into a straight body line.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Lower until your chest is a fist-width from the floor, elbows about 45 degrees from your ribs.
Press the floor away until your arms are straight.
formTips: Think of the body as one plank that moves together.
Keep your wrists stacked under your shoulders at the bottom.
commonMistakes: Sagging hips or piking the hips up.
Only moving the head instead of the chest.
exercises.beginnerModification: Switch to knee push-ups or incline push-ups and build up your reps.

progressions.text: Add a pause at the bottom for one second.
Try diamond push-ups to shift load to the triceps.
Raise your feet with decline push-ups.

exercises.name: Diamond Push-Up
exercises.description: A push-up with the hands close together under the chest. It puts more of the work on the triceps.
instructions: Set up in a push-up position with your index fingers and thumbs close together under your chest.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your ribs.
Lower your chest toward your hands.
Press back up to straight arms.
formTips: If your wrists complain, place the hands a little wider.
Keep the elbows pointing back rather than out.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do them from your knees or with hands slightly apart.

progressions.text: Slow the lowering phase to three seconds.
Move toward archer push-ups.

exercises.name: Decline Push-Up
exercises.description: A push-up with the feet raised. It shifts more load onto the shoulders and upper chest.
instructions: Place your feet on a stable bench or chair and your hands on the floor slightly wider than your shoulders.
Brace your core so your body is one straight line.
Lower your chest toward the floor under control.
Press up until your arms are straight.
formTips: Start with a low surface and raise it only when form is solid.
Keep your gaze slightly ahead of your hands.
commonMistakes: Using a surface that can slide.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lower surface or return to a regular push-up.

progressions.text: Use a higher surface.
Try pike push-ups for a more vertical press.

exercises.name: Pike Push-Up
exercises.description: A push-up in an inverted V shape that trains the shoulders and builds toward handstand strength.
instructions: Start in a downward-dog shape with hips high and hands shoulder-width apart.
Bend your elbows and lower the top of your head toward the floor between your hands.
Press back up to the start position.
formTips: Keep the hips high throughout.
Walk your feet closer to your hands to make it harder.
commonMistakes: Turning it into a regular push-up by dropping the hips.
exercises.beginnerModification: Raise your hands on a sturdy step or bench to reduce the load.

progressions.text: Elevate your feet on a bench.
Practise the wall handstand hold.

exercises.name: Archer Push-Up
exercises.description: A wide push-up where one arm does most of the work while the other arm stays straight. A step toward one-arm push-ups.
instructions: Start in a wide push-up position with hands well outside your shoulders.
Shift your weight to your right hand, bending that elbow while the left arm stays long.
Lower until your chest nears the right hand, then press back to centre.
Repeat on the other side.
formTips: Keep your hips level and square to the floor.
Use as much of the straight arm as you need for balance, and less over time.
commonMistakes: Rotating the torso instead of shifting it.
Going too deep before the shoulder is ready.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do them with hands on a raised surface or shift less far to each side.

progressions.text: Keep the straight arm's fingertips lightly on the floor, then lift them.

exercises.name: Explosive Push-Up
exercises.description: A push-up where you press hard enough for your hands to briefly leave the floor. Builds upper-body power.
instructions: Set up in a strong push-up position.
Lower under control to about chest-fist height.
Press up as fast as you can so your hands lift slightly off the floor.
Land softly with bent elbows and reset before the next rep.
formTips: Do them fresh, early in a session, with full rests.
Land with soft elbows and a braced core.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise fast push-ups from an incline where the hands stay on the surface.

progressions.text: Add a small clap only once the basic version is easy and pain-free.

exercises.name: Wall Handstand Hold
exercises.description: A supported handstand with the feet against a wall. It builds shoulder strength and body awareness upside down.
instructions: Place your hands about 20 cm from the wall and kick up one leg at a time until your heels rest on the wall.
Push tall through your shoulders and squeeze your glutes and core.
Keep the body in a long straight line and breathe steadily.
Come down one leg at a time.
formTips: Practise on a clear floor with a spotter if you are new.
Stop when your form breaks down.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back into a banana shape.
Letting the shoulders sink toward the ears.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start with pike push-ups or a chest-to-wall walk-up hold at a shallow angle.

progressions.text: Reduce wall contact to the toes only.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Squat
exercises.description: The foundation lower-body movement. Sit down between your hips and stand back up.
instructions: Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart and toes slightly turned out.
Brace your core and send your hips back and down.
Lower until your thighs are about parallel or as low as you can with a flat back.
Press through your whole foot to stand tall.
formTips: Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes.
Keep your chest proud and your heels down.
commonMistakes: Lifting the heels off the floor.
exercises.beginnerModification: Squat to a chair and touch it lightly before standing.

progressions.text: Add a two-second pause at the bottom.
Try split squats.
Add a jump with jump squats.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.description: A lunge where you step backward. It is often easier on the knees than stepping forward.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Step one foot back and lower until both knees are about 90 degrees.
Keep most of your weight on the front foot.
Push through the front foot to return to standing.
formTips: Take a step long enough that the front shin stays fairly vertical.
Keep your torso tall.
commonMistakes: Taking a step that is too short.
Letting the front knee cave inward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold a wall or chair for balance and lower only part of the way.

progressions.text: Add dumbbells.
Move to split squats.

exercises.name: Split Squat
exercises.description: A staggered-stance squat where the feet stay planted. Builds single-leg strength and balance.
instructions: Take a long stance with one foot forward and the back heel lifted.
Lower straight down until the back knee hovers just above the floor.
Keep your torso upright.
Press up through the front foot.
formTips: Think straight down and straight up rather than forward and back.
Keep the front foot flat.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold a wall for balance and shorten the range.

progressions.text: Elevate the back foot for a rear-foot-elevated split squat.
Progress toward pistol squats.

exercises.name: Jump Squat
exercises.description: A squat followed by an explosive jump. Trains leg power and is a good conditioning move.
instructions: Set up like a bodyweight squat.
Lower into a quarter to half squat.
Jump up as high as you can, swinging your arms.
Land softly on the whole foot and go straight into the next rep.
formTips: Land quietly with knees and hips bending to absorb force.
Rest fully between sets so every jump is crisp.
commonMistakes: Letting the knees cave inward when landing.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do fast squats that rise onto the toes without leaving the floor.

progressions.text: Try broad jumps for horizontal power.

exercises.name: Broad Jump
exercises.description: A two-foot jump forward for distance. Builds hip and leg power.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Swing your arms back while you bend your hips and knees.
Swing forward and jump out as far as you can.
Land softly with bent knees and stick the landing.
formTips: Stick each landing for a second before resetting.
Use a soft, non-slip surface.
exercises.beginnerModification: Jump shorter distances and focus on soft landings.

progressions.text: Add a small rebound jump straight after landing.

exercises.name: Pistol Squat
exercises.description: A deep squat on one leg with the other leg held out in front. Requires strength, balance and mobility.
instructions: Stand on one leg with the other leg extended in front of you.
Reach your arms forward for balance and sit down slowly on the standing leg.
Lower as deep as you can control.
Press through the whole foot to stand.
formTips: Hold a doorframe or pole for light assistance while learning.
Move slowly on the way down.
commonMistakes: Dropping the last part of the movement.
exercises.beginnerModification: Squat down to a bench on one leg, or use a doorframe for support.

progressions.text: Reduce assistance until you can do the full range without support.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.description: Lift your hips from the floor to strengthen the glutes and back of the legs.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hip-width apart.
Press through your heels and lift your hips until your body forms a line from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes at the top for a second.
Lower slowly.
formTips: Tuck your ribs down so you do not overarch the lower back.
Keep your heels close enough that your shins are vertical at the top.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back at the top.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do a smaller range of motion and hold for less time.

progressions.text: Progress to single-leg bridges.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.description: A glute bridge on one leg. Harder on the glutes and trains hip stability.
instructions: Lie on your back with one foot flat and the other leg extended or held with the knee bent.
Press through the planted heel to lift your hips.
Keep your hips level.
Lower slowly and repeat before switching sides.
formTips: Keep hips level and do not let one side drop.
Squeeze at the top.
commonMistakes: Using the lower back instead of the glutes.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep both feet down and slide one foot forward slightly.

progressions.text: Elevate the working foot on a low step.

exercises.name: Calf Raise
exercises.description: Rise onto the balls of your feet to strengthen the calves.
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, holding a wall for balance if needed.
Press up onto the balls of your feet as high as you can.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower slowly until your heels are near the floor.
formTips: Move slowly and control the lowering.
Keep weight over the big toe side of the foot.
exercises.beginnerModification: Hold a wall or countertop with both hands.

progressions.text: Progress to single-leg calf raises.

exercises.name: Wall Sit
exercises.description: Hold a squat position with your back against a wall. Builds leg endurance.
instructions: Stand with your back against a wall and walk your feet forward.
Slide down until your knees are around 90 degrees.
Keep your back flat against the wall and breathe steadily.
Hold, then slide back up.
formTips: Keep the knees over the ankles, not past the toes.
Rest your hands on your thighs, not on your knees.
exercises.beginnerModification: Sit higher with a smaller knee bend.

progressions.text: Add time in small steps.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.description: A static hold that trains the deep core muscles to keep the body rigid.
instructions: Place your forearms on the floor with elbows under your shoulders.
Extend your legs behind you and rise onto your toes.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your abs so your body is a straight line.
Breathe steadily and hold.
formTips: Stop the set when your form breaks, not when you are exhausted.
Look down at the floor to keep your neck long.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips sag or pike up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Plank from your knees or with hands on a raised surface.

progressions.text: Add a shoulder tap or lift one leg.
Progress to the hollow body hold.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.description: A sideways plank that trains the obliques and hip stabilisers.
instructions: Lie on your side with your elbow under your shoulder and legs stacked.
Lift your hips so your body forms a straight line.
Keep your hips stacked and your neck long.
Hold, then switch sides.
formTips: Push the floor away with your forearm to stay tall.
Keep the hips high.
commonMistakes: Rolling the chest forward or back.
exercises.beginnerModification: Bend your knees and keep them on the floor.

progressions.text: Lift the top leg.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.description: Lie on your back and move opposite arm and leg while your lower back stays anchored. Great for core control.
instructions: Lie on your back with arms straight up and knees bent at 90 degrees over your hips.
Flatten your lower back gently toward the floor.
Lower your right arm and left leg toward the floor slowly.
Return and repeat on the other side.
formTips: Move only as far as you can keep your lower back down.
Exhale as you extend.
commonMistakes: Letting the lower back arch off the floor.
exercises.beginnerModification: Move only the legs, or only the arms, keeping the other pair still.

progressions.text: Add a light weight in the hands.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.description: From hands and knees, reach one arm and the opposite leg long. Trains balance and spinal control.
instructions: Start on hands and knees with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Reach your right arm forward and left leg back until both are in line with your torso.
Keep your hips and shoulders level.
Return and repeat on the other side.
formTips: Imagine balancing a glass of water on your lower back.
Move slowly and pause for a second at full reach.
commonMistakes: Rotating the hips or arching the back.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lift only the leg, or only the arm.

progressions.text: Add an elbow-to-knee crunch under the body.

exercises.name: Bicycle Crunch
exercises.description: An alternating crunch that trains the abs and obliques.
instructions: Lie on your back with hands lightly by your head and knees lifted.
Bring your right elbow toward your left knee while extending the right leg.
Switch sides in a smooth pedalling motion.
Keep your lower back pressed toward the floor.
formTips: Rotate through your ribcage, not by pulling on your neck.
Move at a steady, controlled pace.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep both feet on the floor and do slow alternating toe taps instead.

progressions.text: Slow the tempo and pause at each rotation.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.description: A gymnastics shape where you lie on your back with arms and legs extended and lifted. Builds strong core tension.
instructions: Lie on your back with arms overhead and legs straight.
Press your lower back into the floor and lift your shoulders and legs a few centimetres off the ground.
Keep your ribs down and your body in a shallow banana shape.
Hold and breathe.
formTips: If your lower back lifts, bend the knees or raise the legs higher.
Keep your chin slightly tucked.
commonMistakes: Lifting the legs so low that the back arches.
exercises.beginnerModification: Bend your knees to tuck the legs closer to the chest.

progressions.text: Extend the arms overhead and legs lower.
Try lying leg raises.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Raise
exercises.description: Raise the legs while lying down. Targets the lower abdominal area and hip flexors.
instructions: Lie on your back with hands under your hips.
Keep your legs straight and lift them until they point at the ceiling.
Lower slowly without letting your lower back arch.
Stop just before your heels touch the floor.
formTips: Bend your knees slightly if your lower back lifts.
Lower over three seconds.
exercises.beginnerModification: Bend the knees and raise them toward the chest.

progressions.text: Add a hold at the bottom.

exercises.name: Mountain Climber
exercises.description: Drive the knees toward the chest in a plank. Raises heart rate and trains the core.
instructions: Start in a high plank with hands under shoulders.
Drive one knee toward your chest.
Switch legs quickly in a running motion.
Keep your hips level and shoulders stacked.
formTips: Start slowly and build speed only if your form holds.
Keep your hands firmly planted.
commonMistakes: Letting the shoulders drift behind the hands.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do them slowly, or with hands on a raised surface.

progressions.text: Increase speed for the last few seconds of each interval.

exercises.name: Superman
exercises.description: Lie face down and lift arms and legs slightly to strengthen the back and glutes.
instructions: Lie on your stomach with arms extended overhead.
Gently lift your arms, chest and legs a few centimetres.
Hold for a second, keeping your neck neutral.
Lower slowly.
formTips: Look at the floor to keep your neck long.
Squeeze the glutes rather than cranking the lower back.
commonMistakes: Lifting too high and compressing the lower back.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lift only the arms or only the legs.

progressions.text: Hold each rep for three seconds.

exercises.name: Jumping Jack
exercises.description: A simple full-body cardio move that raises the heart rate quickly and works as a warm-up.
instructions: Stand tall with feet together and arms at your sides.
Jump your feet apart while raising your arms overhead.
Jump back to the start.
Repeat at a steady rhythm.
formTips: Land softly on the balls of your feet.
Keep breathing steadily.
exercises.beginnerModification: Step one foot out at a time instead of jumping.

progressions.text: Try high knees or skater jumps for variety.

exercises.name: High Knees
exercises.description: Run in place while driving the knees up toward hip height.
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Drive your right knee up toward hip height while pumping the opposite arm.
Quickly switch legs.
Stay light on your feet.
formTips: Keep your chest tall and land under your hips.
Scale the height and speed to what you can control.
exercises.beginnerModification: March in place with lifted knees.

progressions.text: Increase speed while keeping the knees high.

exercises.name: Burpee
exercises.description: A full-body conditioning movement combining a squat, plank and jump. Very demanding, so scale it as needed.
instructions: Stand tall, then squat and place your hands on the floor.
Step or jump your feet back into a plank.
Step or jump your feet back toward your hands.
Stand and jump up with arms overhead.
formTips: Choose a pace you can keep with control.
Keep your core braced in the plank.
commonMistakes: Collapsing the lower back in the plank.
exercises.beginnerModification: Step back and forward without the push-up or jump.

progressions.text: Add a push-up in the plank.

exercises.name: Skater Jump
exercises.description: Bound side to side from one foot to the other like a speed skater. Trains lateral power and balance.
instructions: Stand on one leg with a slight knee bend.
Bound sideways to the other leg, landing softly.
Let your free leg sweep behind you.
Bound back and repeat.
formTips: Land softly and pause briefly to control the landing.
Start with a short bound.
commonMistakes: Losing balance from too big a bound.
exercises.beginnerModification: Step side to side without jumping.

progressions.text: Add a small hop on each landing.

exercises.name: Bear Crawl
exercises.description: Crawl on hands and toes with the knees hovering off the floor. Great for shoulders and core.
instructions: Start on hands and toes with knees hovering a few centimetres off the floor.
Move the opposite hand and foot forward together.
Keep your hips low and your back flat.
Crawl forward, then backward.
formTips: Take small controlled steps.
Keep your gaze slightly ahead.
commonMistakes: Moving too quickly with sloppy form.
exercises.beginnerModification: Rock forward and back in the bear position without crawling.

progressions.text: Crawl backward or sideways.

exercises.name: Pull-Up
exercises.description: Hang from a bar and pull your chin above it. A benchmark upper-body strength exercise.
instructions: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulders.
Pull your shoulder blades down and back.
Pull your chest toward the bar until your chin clears it.
Lower under control to a full hang.
formTips: Start each rep from a controlled hang.
Squeeze your glutes and keep your legs still.
commonMistakes: Shortening the range at the bottom.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a resistance band for assistance or do slow lowerings from the top.

progressions.text: Add a pause at the top.
Progress to weighted pull-ups.

exercises.name: Chin-Up
exercises.description: A pull-up with an underhand grip that involves the biceps more.
instructions: Hang from a bar with palms facing you and hands shoulder-width apart.
Pull your shoulder blades down.
Pull your chin above the bar, keeping elbows pointing down.
Lower to a full hang.
formTips: Control the way down for two to three seconds.
Keep the chest up.
commonMistakes: Stopping short of a full hang.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a band for assistance or step up and lower slowly.

progressions.text: Add a pause at the top.

exercises.name: Band Pull-Apart
exercises.description: Pull a resistance band apart at chest height. Strengthens the upper back and improves posture.
instructions: Hold a band in front of you at chest height with arms straight.
Pull the band apart by squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause when your arms are out to the sides.
Return slowly.
formTips: Keep your ribs down and shoulders away from the ears.
Use a lighter band and better form before a heavier band.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a light band and a smaller range.

progressions.text: Use a slightly heavier band.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Row
exercises.description: Pull a band toward your torso, anchored in front of you. A simple back exercise you can do anywhere.
instructions: Anchor the band securely at chest height or loop it around your feet while seated.
Hold the ends with arms extended and shoulders down.
Pull your elbows back and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Return slowly.
formTips: Check that the anchor cannot slip.
Keep your torso still and tall.
commonMistakes: Leaning back to cheat the pull.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter band or step closer to the anchor.

progressions.text: Use a heavier band or pause for two seconds at the squeeze.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Squat
exercises.description: A squat with a band under your feet for extra resistance.
instructions: Stand on the middle of the band and hold the ends at your shoulders.
Squat down with a tall chest.
Drive up through your whole foot.
Keep the band tight throughout.
formTips: Keep knees tracking over the toes.
Ensure the band is not frayed before use.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter band or squat to a chair.

progressions.text: Use a heavier band.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Row
exercises.description: Row a dumbbell toward your hip while supported on a bench or chair. Builds the upper back.
instructions: Place one hand and knee on a bench or chair and hold a dumbbell in the other hand.
Keep your back flat and your hips square.
Pull the dumbbell toward your hip, leading with the elbow.
Lower with control.
formTips: Keep your neck in line with your spine.
Pull with your back, not by twisting.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter weight and a shorter range.

progressions.text: Increase the weight or add a pause.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
exercises.description: Press dumbbells overhead to build shoulder strength.
instructions: Stand or sit tall holding dumbbells at shoulder height with palms forward.
Brace your core.
Press the weights overhead until your arms are straight.
Lower back to shoulder height slowly.
formTips: Keep your ribs down and avoid arching the back.
Press slightly in front of you rather than straight out to the side.
commonMistakes: Using a weight that is too heavy.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use lighter weights or do it seated with back support.

progressions.text: Use heavier dumbbells.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Curl
exercises.description: Curl dumbbells to build the front of the arms.
instructions: Stand tall holding dumbbells at your sides with palms forward.
Keep your elbows close to your ribs.
Curl the weights up toward your shoulders.
Lower slowly.
formTips: Do not swing the torso.
Squeeze at the top.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use lighter weights.

progressions.text: Slow the lowering to three seconds.

exercises.name: Bench Dip
exercises.description: Lower and raise your body with hands on a bench behind you. Builds the triceps.
instructions: Sit on the edge of a sturdy bench and place your hands beside your hips.
Slide your hips off the bench with knees bent.
Lower until your elbows reach about 90 degrees.
Press back up.
formTips: Keep your hips close to the bench.
Stop if you feel pinching in the front of the shoulder.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep your knees bent and feet close to your body.

progressions.text: Extend your legs further away.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.description: Hold one dumbbell at your chest while squatting. The weight helps you stay upright.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell vertically against your chest.
Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulders.
Squat down between your knees.
Drive up through your heels and midfoot.
formTips: Keep your elbows inside your knees at the bottom.
Keep the weight close to your body.
commonMistakes: Letting the weight pull you forward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter weight and a shallower squat.

progressions.text: Use a heavier dumbbell.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.description: Hinge at the hips with dumbbells to train the hamstrings and glutes.
instructions: Stand tall holding dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Push your hips back with a soft bend in the knees.
Lower the weights along your legs until you feel a hamstring stretch.
Squeeze your glutes to stand tall again.
formTips: Keep your back flat and the dumbbells close.
Think about pushing your hips back, not bending forward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practise the hinge without weight, touching a wall behind you with your hips.

progressions.text: Use heavier dumbbells.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.description: Press dumbbells up while lying on a flat bench. A classic chest exercise.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand at chest level.
Plant your feet firmly and keep your shoulder blades pinched.
Press the weights up until your arms are straight.
Lower slowly to chest level.
formTips: Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows.
Use a weight you can control on every rep.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use lighter weights or do floor presses.

progressions.text: Use heavier dumbbells.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
exercises.description: Pull a bar down toward your chest on a cable machine. Builds the upper back and helps you progress toward pull-ups.
instructions: Sit at the machine with thighs secured under the pads.
Grab the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Pull the bar to your upper chest, leading with your elbows.
Return the bar slowly.
formTips: Sit tall and do not lean back excessively.
Choose a weight you can control.
commonMistakes: Pulling the bar behind the neck.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter weight and a smaller range.

progressions.text: Work toward pull-ups.

exercises.name: Cat-Cow
exercises.description: Move the spine between rounding and arching on hands and knees. A gentle spinal warm-up.
instructions: Start on hands and knees.
Inhale, drop your belly and lift your chest and tailbone.
Exhale, round your back and tuck your chin.
Flow between the two slowly.
formTips: Move with your breath.
Keep the movement comfortable.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a smaller range and pause on the way.

progressions.text: Add slow rotations of the ribcage.

exercises.name: World's Greatest Stretch
exercises.description: A flowing lunge and rotation that opens the hips, hamstrings and upper back.
instructions: Step into a long lunge with both hands on the floor inside the front foot.
Rotate the chest toward the front leg and reach that arm up.
Return the hand to the floor.
Step through to the other side.
formTips: Breathe out as you rotate.
Keep the movement smooth.
exercises.beginnerModification: Keep the back knee on the floor.

progressions.text: Add a hamstring stretch by straightening the front leg.

exercises.name: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.description: Stretch the front of the hip in a half-kneeling position.
instructions: Kneel on one knee with the other foot forward.
Tuck your pelvis under and squeeze the back glute.
Shift your weight forward gently.
Hold, breathing steadily, then switch.
formTips: Tuck the pelvis rather than arching the back.
Ease into the stretch.
exercises.beginnerModification: Pad the kneeling knee and take a shorter stance.

progressions.text: Raise the same-side arm overhead.

exercises.name: Thoracic Open Book
exercises.description: Rotate the upper back while lying on your side. Improves upper-back mobility.
instructions: Lie on your side with knees bent and arms out in front.
Lift your top arm and open it toward the other side, following with your eyes.
Pause when you feel a comfortable stretch.
Return and repeat.
formTips: Keep your knees together.
Breathe out as you open.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a smaller range or place a pillow between the knees.

progressions.text: Hold the open position for several breaths.

exercises.name: Child's Pose
exercises.description: A resting stretch that gently lengthens the back and hips.
instructions: Kneel and sit back toward your heels.
Reach your arms forward along the floor.
Rest your forehead down.
Breathe slowly.
formTips: Widen your knees if it is more comfortable.
Relax your jaw and shoulders.
exercises.beginnerModification: Place a cushion between your hips and heels.

progressions.text: Walk your hands to each side to stretch the sides of the torso.

exercises.name: Arm Circles
exercises.description: Circle the arms to warm up the shoulders.
instructions: Stand tall with your arms out to the sides.
Make small circles, gradually getting bigger.
Reverse the direction after several seconds.
Keep your shoulders relaxed.
formTips: Keep the neck relaxed.
Stay within a comfortable range.
exercises.beginnerModification: Make smaller circles.

progressions.text: Add a slow pulse at the top of each circle.
